function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with a given portion size to track dietary intake. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log, such as 'apple', 'bread', or 'chicken breast'.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, specified in the unit given by portion_unit. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount, such as 'cup', 'grams', or 'slice'.

meal_type.description: The type of meal or snack this food item is being logged for.

log_date.description: The date and time when the food was consumed, in ISO 8601 format such as 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ'.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to log foods. They mention:

"I had 8 pieces of frozen mango and a chai tea."

Also earlier they had "two slices of pepperoni pizza and a coffee".

We need to call the function twice? Actually we can log each item separately. We have multiple items per meal maybe. But the tool expects one food at a time. So we should make separate calls for each food item. For each call specify food_name, portion_amount, portion_unit, meal_type (default snack). Also optionally log_date but not needed if omitted; defaults to null.

Thus produce JSON calls for each item:

First: 8 pieces of frozen mango -> food_name: "frozen mango"? Or just "mango". Portion_amount: 8, portion_unit: piece. Meal_type unspecified so default snack.

Second: chai tea - it's beverage. Food_name: "chai tea". Portion_amount: ??? Not specified. Maybe assume standard cup? Could ask clarifying question. But likely they'd want to log it anyway. Since no quantity given, perhaps use 1 cup. We'll set portion_amount=1, portion_unit="cup".

Third: two slices of pepperoni pizza -> food_name: "pepperoni pizza slice". Portion_amount:2, portion_unit:"slice"

Fourth: coffee -> again unknown quantity. Use 1 cup.

But might also combine into single logs? The instructions say "Logs a food item with a given portion size." So each call logs an individual item. So four calls.

Let's do them sequentially. Provide output accordingly.
